title: Do concussions cause early death?
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck discuss concussions: what they are (brain striking the inside of the skull), symptoms and how to assess an injured player, the NFL's history of downplaying concussions (John McKay and Ralph Wenzel, the NFL dementia care plan, new return-to-play rule), long-term risks including chronic traumatic encephalopathy and second impact syndrome, research by Chris Nowinski, Robert Cantu and the Center for the Study of Traumatic Encephalopathy, youth and high school football, treatment and post-concussion syndrome, and personal anecdotes. The episode closes with listener mail and Kiva plugs.

entities.name: Center for the Study of Traumatic Encephalopathy

segments.title: Opening banter and what a concussion is
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about concussions being in the news, then Josh explains a concussion as the brain slapping the inside of the skull, and they joke about protective designs.

segments.title: Concussion symptoms and assessment
segments.summary: Chuck lists outward and internal symptoms of concussion, including nausea, confusion, light and sound sensitivity, headache, and amnesia, and describes sideline questioning used to assess players.

segments.title: NFL concussion history and dementia benefits
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the NFL's history of downplaying concussions, the case of John McKay and Ralph Wenzel on the San Diego Chargers, and the NFL plan, begun after McKay's wife's letter, that offers care benefits to families of players with early dementia.

segments.title: NFL return-to-play rule and team doctors
segments.summary: The hosts describe a new NFL rule that bars players with amnesia, poor balance or abnormal neurological exams from returning to the game, and note that independent doctors will perform post-game tests rather than team doctors.

segments.title: Sports Legacy Institute and brain research
segments.summary: Chris Nowinski's history of concussions and his work with Robert Cantu at the Sports Legacy Institute, which collects donated brains for study at the Center for the Study of Traumatic Encephalopathy, finding Alzheimer's-like brains in younger former players, including Andre Waters and Ted Johnson.

segments.title: Second impact syndrome and brain herniation
segments.summary: The hosts explain that a second concussion before the first heals can cause second impact syndrome, in which the brain swells, leading to herniation and death, and they discuss the risk of brain-stem failure.

segments.title: Youth football, other sports and treatment
segments.summary: The hosts discuss high school football concussions, the risks of other sports and activities, and treatment advice: stop activity immediately, see a doctor, note that CT and MRI scans cannot directly show a concussion, and rest is not harmful. They also cover post-concussion syndrome.
topics: CT scan and MRI for concussion

segments.title: Structural vs functional debate and personal anecdotes
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether concussion damage is structural or functional, mention protein tangles, and share personal concussion stories, including Chuck being hit with a softball bat and Josh's rifle recoil incident.

segments.title: Listener mail: Will and Katie
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh read a letter from twelve-year-old Will in Arlington, Virginia about flirting and a poem from high school freshman Katie in Florida about a bird that hit a window.

segments.title: Kiva plug and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts promote the Stuff You Should Know Kiva lending team and invite listeners to email the show.
